narrative: The model estimates a 10% probability that you will fail your final year. That is a low risk, not a certainty, but the school’s rule has flagged you for remedial courses as an early warning. The strongest signals in your profile actually point toward passing, which is why the estimated failure risk is only 10%. Your past class failures are the most influential factor: you have none, compared with an average of zero among students who passed, so this strongly supports passing. Your intention to pursue higher education is the second most influential: you said yes, and every passing student in the comparison group also said yes. Weekly study time is third: you study 2–5 hours, the most common pattern among passing students at 55.2%, so it supports passing but not dramatically. The remaining 10% risk comes from weaker factors rather than these top three. To improve, keep your record free of failures, protect your plan for higher education, and consider increasing study time beyond 2–5 hours, especially in the subject most at risk. You also do not receive family educational support, paid classes or school support, and you lack home internet, all of which are less common among passers; ask about school resources and internet access. Maintaining zero absences and your very good family relationships will help too.
